newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears Hoechst/BASF polypropylene venture.
newsitem.headline: EU clears Hoechst/BASF polypropylene venture.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it had cleared a proposal by German Chemical companies Hoechst and BASF to pool their west European polypropylene activities in a new joint venture called Targor.

The Commission said in a statement that BASF will be able to exercise full control in the new company despite it being a 50-50 venture because of "various dispositions contained in the founding agreement".

It said that the operation had to be seen in the context of the restructuring of the sector, citing the creation of the Montell joint venture between Shell and Montedison, Borealis between Neste and Statoil and Appryl between BP and Elf Atochem.

The Commission said that although the restructuring deals had led to Montell, Targor and Borealis, the three largest producers, accounting for more than half of the polypropylene supply, it did not give rise to concerns as there were still a large number of competitors. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
